pearson-test-with-estimated-parameters.prompt: In the paired four-cell model, can changing $\theta$ make the first two fitted probabilities unequal?
pearson-test-with-estimated-parameters.answer: No. They are both $\theta$. Their within-pair difference remains a lack-of-fit direction.

pitman-koopman-darmois-informal-form.title: A fixed total
pitman-koopman-darmois-informal-form.prompt: Two iid Poisson samples have equal size and equal sum but different order. Can their likelihood ratio depend on the common rate?
pitman-koopman-darmois-informal-form.answer: No. The rate-dependent factor $\exp(-n\lambda)\lambda^{\sum x}$ is identical, leaving a data-only ratio.

pitman-koopman-darmois-informal-form.title: The support condition
pitman-koopman-darmois-informal-form.prompt: Why does a sufficient maximum for U(0,θ) fail to establish the regular exponential-family converse?
pitman-koopman-darmois-informal-form.answer: The set of possible observations depends on θ through 0<x<θ, violating the common-support condition.

posterior-class-probability.title: Two layers of uncertainty
posterior-class-probability.prompt: A logistic regression reports a class probability of 0.7 at a covariate value. Does that number already average over posterior uncertainty in the coefficients?
posterior-class-probability.answer: No. A logistic probability evaluated at one coefficient vector is a conditional class probability. The posterior class probability averages that logistic probability over the posterior distribution of the coefficients.

posterior-class-probability.title: A cost threshold
posterior-class-probability.prompt: If a false positive costs twice a false negative, what posterior class-1 probability is needed to choose class 1?
posterior-class-probability.answer: Choose class 1 when 2(1−p)<p, so p>2/3, with a tie at 2/3.

posterior-predictive-target.title: Parameter or outcome?
posterior-predictive-target.prompt: Is drawing θ from Beta(3,9) alone a posterior predictive draw of the four-item count K?
posterior-predictive-target.answer: No. After drawing θ, draw K from Binomial(4,θ). The second step adds the future batch variation.

posterior-predictive-target.title: Shared uncertainty
posterior-predictive-target.prompt: Two future binary items are drawn from one θ after θ is drawn from Beta(3,9). Are the items independent in the posterior predictive distribution?
posterior-predictive-target.answer: They are conditionally independent given θ. In the predictive distribution they are dependent, and their covariance equals Var(θ) = 3/208, which is positive.

power-function.title: Null and alternative
power-function.prompt: For the binomial threshold X≥9, is 0.010742 a p-value from observed data or a design property?
power-function.answer: It is the rejection probability at p=0.5, hence the size for that point null. It is specified by the design and sampling model.

power-function.title: A larger sample
power-function.prompt: The normal test uses σ = 2 and a one-unit departure. What is the noncentrality at n = 100?
power-function.answer: It is √100 × 1/2 = 5, twice the noncentrality 2.5 at n = 25. With the same critical value 1.644854 the power is 0.999603.

predictive-variance-decomposition.title: The between-means term
predictive-variance-decomposition.prompt: A mixture assigns equal probabilities to conditional means −1 and 1, each with variance 2. What is its variance?
predictive-variance-decomposition.answer: The mean is zero. The mean conditional variance is 2 and the variance of the conditional means is 1, so the total is 3.

predictive-variance-decomposition.title: A varying plug-in variance
predictive-variance-decomposition.prompt: Does dropping parameter uncertainty prove that any chosen plug-in variance underestimates predictive variance?
predictive-variance-decomposition.answer: No. A chosen conditional variance can exceed or fall below its posterior average. The nonnegative omitted term alone compares the full variance with the averaged conditional variance.

principal-component-directions.title: A tied covariance
principal-component-directions.prompt: If S=2I in two dimensions, which unit vector maximises variance?
principal-component-directions.answer: Every unit vector does: aᵀSa=2aᵀa=2. The leading eigenspace is the whole plane and no unique first axis is identified.

principal-component-directions.title: A zero eigenvalue
principal-component-directions.prompt: What does a zero eigenvalue imply for its sample score column after centring?
principal-component-directions.answer: Its sample variance is zero and its mean is zero, so every score in that column is zero.

prior-sensitivity.title: Prior concentration
prior-sensitivity.prompt: For a beta prior with concentration 20 and n=80 binomial trials, what is the prior weight in the posterior mean?

prior-sensitivity.title: A support restriction
prior-sensitivity.prompt: A prior puts probability zero on $\theta>0.8$. Can ordinary Bayesian updating with finite likelihood values put positive posterior mass there?
prior-sensitivity.answer: No. Multiplying a zero prior density by a finite likelihood leaves it zero, so the restriction survives updating.

properties-of-a-probability.title: Disjoint or independent
properties-of-a-probability.prompt: Can two disjoint events each with probability 0.2 be independent?
properties-of-a-probability.answer: No. Their intersection has probability zero, but independence would require probability 0.2×0.2=0.04.

properties-of-a-probability.title: A union bound
properties-of-a-probability.prompt: Three events have probabilities 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3. What upper bound holds for their union without an independence assumption?
properties-of-a-probability.answer: The union probability is at most 0.6, the sum of the three probabilities.

quasi-likelihood.title: Dispersion cancellation
quasi-likelihood.prompt: If a common dispersion is doubled, how do the quasi-score roots and model-based standard errors change?
quasi-likelihood.answer: The roots stay the same. Covariance doubles and standard errors multiply by $\sqrt2$, with the mean and working variance function held fixed.

quasi-likelihood.title: Binary support restriction
quasi-likelihood.prompt: Can a single Bernoulli variable with mean $0.4$ have variance $2\mu(1-\mu)$?
quasi-likelihood.answer: No. Its variance is forced to be $0.4(0.6)=0.24$ by $Y^2=Y$. The proposed value $0.48$ violates that identity.

r-s-distribution-interface.title: Density or probability?
r-s-distribution-interface.prompt: The beta density at 0.25 is 3.097243. Is this the probability that θ equals 0.25?
r-s-distribution-interface.answer: No. A continuous variable assigns probability zero to one point; a density is integrated over an interval to obtain probability.

r-s-distribution-interface.title: A cumulative probability at another point
r-s-distribution-interface.prompt: For a Beta(3,9) variable, pbeta(0.1, 3, 9) returns 0.089562. What probability is that?
r-s-distribution-interface.answer: It is $P(\theta \le 0.1)$. The prefix p returns a cumulative probability. It is not the density at 0.1, and it is not the probability of the point 0.5 used in the worked CDF.

radial-basis-function-kernel.title: Two parameter conventions
radial-basis-function-kernel.prompt: What gamma corresponds to length scale ell=2?

radial-basis-function-kernel.title: The zero-width limit
radial-basis-function-kernel.prompt: For three distinct fixed inputs, what does the Gram matrix approach as gamma grows without bound?
radial-basis-function-kernel.answer: Each diagonal stays one and every off-diagonal entry tends to zero, so the limit is the 3×3 identity matrix.

random-seed.title: A short modulus
random-seed.prompt: The map S ↦ (5S+1) mod 7 is started at 5. What is the next state, and does full period on modulus 8 settle the period here?
random-seed.answer: The next state is 5, because (5×5+1) mod 7 = 5, so 5 is a fixed point. Full period on modulus 8 does not determine the period on modulus 7.

random-seed.title: Repeated seeds
random-seed.prompt: If every replicate resets the same seed and executes the same calls, do the replicates estimate independent simulation variability?
random-seed.answer: No. They replay the same deterministic stream. Independent-replicate variation requires a suitable advancing stream or explicitly constructed substreams.

random-walk-with-drift.title: Time-dependent variance
random-walk-with-drift.prompt: Why is an iid-increment random walk with positive increment variance not covariance-stationary?
random-walk-with-drift.answer: Its variance is $n\sigma^2$, which depends on time. Stationary increments do not make its levels stationary.

random-walk-with-drift.title: Shared increments
random-walk-with-drift.prompt: If increment variance is $3$, what is $\operatorname{Cov}(S_4,S_{10})$ for a deterministic start?
random-walk-with-drift.answer: The sums share four increments, so the covariance is $4\times3=12$.

range.title: A value inside the endpoints
range.prompt: The sample minimum is $-2$ and maximum is $5$. An observation equal to $1$ is appended. What is the range?
range.answer: $5-(-2)=7$. The appended value changes neither endpoint.

range.title: Changing units
range.prompt: A temperature sample has range $8$ degrees Celsius. What is its Fahrenheit range under $F=32+1.8C$?
range.answer: $1.8\times8=14.4$ degrees Fahrenheit. The additive constant cancels.

rank-bound.title: Enough rows is not sufficient
rank-bound.prompt: With n=30 and p=5, must the sample covariance be invertible?
rank-bound.answer: No. The sample-size bound allows rank 5, but linearly dependent centred columns can still make it singular.

rank-bound.title: Group centring
rank-bound.prompt: A pooled scatter matrix uses 40 observations in four nonempty groups. What is its observation-space rank bound?
rank-bound.answer: It is at most 40−4=36, and also cannot exceed the number of variables.

rank-distance.title: Maximum and sum disagree
rank-distance.prompt: Rank-gap vectors (5,2) and (6,0) are compared. Which is closer under the maximum of absolute gaps, and which is closer under the sum?
rank-distance.answer: The maximum distances are 5 and 6, so (5,2) is closer under the maximum. The sums are 7 and 6, so (6,0) is closer under the sum.

rank-distance.title: Reversing a scale
rank-distance.prompt: With four pooled untied values, ranks change from r to 5−r under a decreasing transformation. Do absolute rank gaps change?

rat-tumour-data.title: Zero affected animals
rat-tumour-data.prompt: With fixed positive $\alpha,\beta$, does a group with zero affected animals have posterior mean zero?
rat-tumour-data.answer: No. Its posterior mean is $\alpha/(\alpha+\beta+n)>0$. The model still assigns positive rates through the proper beta prior.

rat-tumour-data.title: Two kinds of uncertainty
rat-tumour-data.prompt: Why is the sample standard deviation of study fractions not simply the standard deviation of the underlying study rates?
rat-tumour-data.answer: Observed fractions also vary because each group contains finitely many binomial outcomes. Between-study heterogeneity and within-study sampling error both contribute.

reading-a-log-linear-coefficient.title: An interaction contrast
reading-a-log-linear-coefficient.prompt: The log-mean contrast in x is 0.2 − 0.1z. What factor does a one-unit increase in x produce at z = 4?
reading-a-log-linear-coefficient.answer: The contrast is 0.2 − 0.4 = −0.2, so the factor is exp(−0.2) = 0.818731. The coefficient 0.2 is the log-mean change at z = 0.

reading-a-log-linear-coefficient.title: Count or rate?
reading-a-log-linear-coefficient.prompt: Under a Poisson log-exposure offset, does doubling exposure change the predicted rate when all covariates are fixed?
reading-a-log-linear-coefficient.answer: No. The rate stays fixed and the expected count doubles because mean count equals exposure times rate.

regression-tree.title: A constant leaf
regression-tree.prompt: For a leaf containing responses 2,4,9, what is the squared-error prediction?

regression-tree.title: Training loss
regression-tree.prompt: Can splitting a nonempty leaf into two nonempty leaves increase the minimum training sum of squares when each child uses its mean?
regression-tree.answer: No. Using the parent mean in both children is an available candidate, and optimising their means can only maintain or decrease that error.

regression-when-p-n.title: Singularity from dimensions
regression-when-p-n.prompt: An $8\times12$ design matrix includes all coefficients. Can $X^TX$ be invertible?
regression-when-p-n.answer: No. Its rank is at most $8$, below its dimension $12$; the coefficient null space has dimension at least $4$.

regression-when-p-n.title: Zero training error
regression-when-p-n.prompt: Does a full-row-rank design with more columns than rows guarantee that every response vector can be fitted exactly?
regression-when-p-n.answer: Yes: its column space is all of $\mathbb R^n$. This guarantees interpolation of the training responses, without guaranteeing accurate future predictions.

reliability-function.title: Dependence of backups
reliability-function.prompt: Two backup components each work with probability 0.9 and their states always agree. What is their parallel reliability?
reliability-function.answer: It is 0.9, since both succeed and fail together. The independent-components value 0.99 does not apply.

reliability-function.title: A series of three
reliability-function.prompt: Independent components work with probabilities 0.9, 0.8 and 0.7. What is the reliability of the series system that needs every component?

residuals-in-a-glm.title: Dispersion scaling
residuals-in-a-glm.prompt: If an unscaled Pearson residual is $4$ and estimated dispersion is $4$, what is the dispersion-scaled residual?

residuals-in-a-glm.title: Deviance total
residuals-in-a-glm.prompt: Four unscaled deviance residuals are $-1,0,2,-3$. What is their total deviance contribution?
residuals-in-a-glm.answer: The sum of their squares is $1+0+4+9=14$. The signs describe direction but do not enter the deviance total.

sample-size-for-a-confidence-interval.title: Rounding a bound
sample-size-for-a-confidence-interval.prompt: A width calculation gives $n\ge100.2$. Is a sample of $100$ sufficient?
sample-size-for-a-confidence-interval.answer: No. The smallest integer satisfying the inequality is $101$.

sample-size-for-a-confidence-interval.title: Tripling precision
sample-size-for-a-confidence-interval.prompt: How does the continuous sample-size requirement change when the target half-width is divided by $3$?
sample-size-for-a-confidence-interval.answer: It is multiplied by $3^2=9$, holding confidence and spread fixed.

sampling-distribution-of-the-ols-estimat.title: Residual dimension
sampling-distribution-of-the-ols-estimat.prompt: With 12 responses and a rank-four Gaussian regression design, what is the residual chi-square degrees of freedom?
sampling-distribution-of-the-ols-estimat.answer: It is 12−4=8. All four fitted mean parameters use residual dimensions.

sampling-distribution-of-the-ols-estimat.title: Conditioning
sampling-distribution-of-the-ols-estimat.prompt: In the OLS sampling distribution, what is random when X and β are fixed?
sampling-distribution-of-the-ols-estimat.answer: The error vector, hence the response vector and its coefficient estimate, is random. The displayed law is not a posterior distribution of β.

sampling-distribution-of-the-regression-.title: Away from the centre
sampling-distribution-of-the-regression-.prompt: For x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and σ = 2, what is the variance of the fitted mean at x = 5?
sampling-distribution-of-the-regression-.answer: It is 4{1/5 + (5−3)²/10} = 2.400, three times the variance 0.800 at the centre x = 3.

sampling-distribution-of-the-regression-.title: A more spread design
sampling-distribution-of-the-regression-.prompt: Every centred predictor deviation is doubled, while n and σ stay fixed. What happens to Sxx and to the slope variance?
sampling-distribution-of-the-regression-.answer: Sxx is multiplied by four, and the slope variance is divided by four.

sampling-law-of-the-normal-mean-and-scat.title: Degrees of freedom and rank
sampling-law-of-the-normal-mean-and-scat.prompt: For five bivariate normal observations, how many Wishart degrees of freedom does the centred scatter have?
sampling-law-of-the-normal-mean-and-scat.answer: It has five minus one, or four. The centring operation removes one observation-space direction.

sampling-law-of-the-normal-mean-and-scat.title: Different scales
sampling-law-of-the-normal-mean-and-scat.prompt: With the displayed Σ and n=10, why are 11.000 and 1.100 both relevant variances?
sampling-law-of-the-normal-mean-and-scat.answer: 11.000 is the variance of an individual contrast X1−X2. The variance of the mean contrast divides it by ten, giving 1.100.

scaling.title: Variance units
scaling.prompt: Multiplying a feature by 10 multiplies its variance and its covariance with an unchanged feature by what factors?
scaling.answer: The variance is multiplied by 100 and that covariance is multiplied by 10.

scaling.title: Constant columns
scaling.prompt: Why cannot a constant training column be standardised to sample variance one?
scaling.answer: Its sample standard deviation is zero. Dividing by that scale is undefined, and centring alone leaves a zero column.

scree-plot.title: An explicit percentage rule
scree-plot.prompt: For eigenvalues 5,2,1,0.5,0.5, how many components are required to explain at least 90%?
scree-plot.answer: Four components: the first three explain 8/9, below 90%, and the first four explain 8.5/9, above 90%.

scree-plot.title: A correlation reference
scree-plot.prompt: Why is one the average eigenvalue in a p-variable correlation PCA?
scree-plot.answer: The correlation matrix has trace p, equal to the sum of its p eigenvalues, so their average is one.

sensitivity-and-specificity.title: Zero denominators
sensitivity-and-specificity.prompt: A study has no reference-positive cases. Can it estimate sensitivity?
sensitivity-and-specificity.answer: No. The sensitivity denominator is the number of reference-positive cases, which is zero.

sensitivity-and-specificity.title: Threshold direction
sensitivity-and-specificity.prompt: On a fixed sample, can raising a positive-call threshold decrease specificity?
sensitivity-and-specificity.answer: No. Raising the threshold can only maintain or reduce false-positive calls, so specificity cannot decrease.

sign-test.title: A small exact tail
sign-test.prompt: Six untied pairs are judged by a positive-direction sign test. Under a fair-sign null, what is P(N+ at least 5)?

sign-test.title: One huge increase
sign-test.prompt: If the largest positive difference becomes a thousand times larger without changing any sign, does the sign-test statistic change?
sign-test.answer: No. The positive-sign count is unchanged.

simple-random-sample.title: A complete enumeration
simple-random-sample.prompt: How many SRS samples of size three can be selected from five labelled units?
simple-random-sample.answer: There are choose(5,3)=10 equally likely subsets.

simple-random-sample.title: A census variance
simple-random-sample.prompt: What is the sampling variance of the mean when n=N under this design?
simple-random-sample.answer: It is zero, because the finite-population correction 1−n/N is zero.

simple-variables-and-expectation.title: Disjoint refinement
simple-variables-and-expectation.prompt: An event of probability $0.4$ has attached value $3$. It is split into events with probabilities $0.1$ and $0.3$, both still carrying value $3$. Does its contribution change?

simple-variables-and-expectation.title: A countable range
simple-variables-and-expectation.prompt: Is a geometric random variable with possible values $1,2,3,\ldots$ simple?
simple-variables-and-expectation.answer: No. Its range is infinite. Its bounded truncations are simple and can approximate it increasingly.

simultaneous-confidence-statements.title: Protecting three comparisons
simultaneous-confidence-statements.prompt: At family error level $0.05$, what per-interval error bound does Bonferroni use for three prespecified contrasts?
simultaneous-confidence-statements.answer: $0.05/3$ per interval. The sum of their failure-probability bounds is $0.05$.

simultaneous-confidence-statements.title: A zero direction
simultaneous-confidence-statements.prompt: What interval does the ellipsoid projection give when $a=0$?
simultaneous-confidence-statements.answer: The contrast is identically zero and its half-width is zero, so the interval is the singleton $\{0\}$.

singular-value-decomposition.title: The covariance divisor
singular-value-decomposition.prompt: A centred matrix with n=6 has singular value 10. What sample covariance eigenvalue does it produce?

singular-value-decomposition.title: Compact dimensions
singular-value-decomposition.prompt: A 20×5 matrix has rank 3. What are the dimensions of its compact U, Sigma and V?

sleep-deprivation-data.title: Counting independent subjects
sleep-deprivation-data.prompt: Why are the 180 records not equivalent to 180 independently sampled subjects in the mixed model?
sleep-deprivation-data.answer: Ten records share each subject’s intercept and slope effects. The model has eighteen subject-level clusters, with dependence among records in each cluster.

sleep-deprivation-data.title: Conditional or marginal variance?
sleep-deprivation-data.prompt: Does increasing marginal variance over days imply that the model’s residual variance σ² increases?
sleep-deprivation-data.answer: No. A random slope contributes d²G11 and 2dG01 to marginal variance even with constant conditional residual variance σ².

slope-t-pivot.title: Two fitted parameters
slope-t-pivot.prompt: Why does simple regression use n−2 degrees of freedom rather than n−1 in its slope t pivot?
slope-t-pivot.answer: Both intercept and slope are fitted, leaving n−2 independent residual directions in the Gaussian model.

slope-t-pivot.title: A shifted origin
slope-t-pivot.prompt: Would subtracting 100 from every predictor value change the slope statistic for a zero slope?
slope-t-pivot.answer: No. Centred predictor differences, Sxx, fitted slope and residual standard deviation are all unchanged.

softmax-is-multinomial-logistic-regressi.title: Reference odds
softmax-is-multinomial-logistic-regressi.prompt: For probabilities (1/6,1/3,1/2), what are the odds of class3 relative to class1?
softmax-is-multinomial-logistic-regressi.answer: They are (1/2)/(1/6)=3, with log odds log(3).

softmax-is-multinomial-logistic-regressi.title: Gradient sum
softmax-is-multinomial-logistic-regressi.prompt: Why do the score derivatives of one-observation cross-entropy sum to zero?
softmax-is-multinomial-logistic-regressi.answer: They sum to the total predicted probability, one, minus the total of the one-hot indicators, also one. This agrees with invariance to a common score shift.

spatial-poisson-process.title: Overlapping windows
spatial-poisson-process.prompt: Are counts in overlapping inspection windows necessarily independent in a Poisson process?
spatial-poisson-process.answer: No. They share the count in their intersection. Their covariance equals the intensity measure of that intersection.

spatial-poisson-process.title: Space and time
spatial-poisson-process.prompt: Why does the planar nearest-point survival contain r² rather than r?
spatial-poisson-process.answer: The event is an empty disk, whose area is πr². A one-dimensional interval instead has length proportional to r.

spline.title: Count the basis
spline.prompt: A cubic spline has three strictly interior knots and two separate fixed boundaries. What are the unconstrained and natural dimensions?
spline.answer: The unconstrained dimension is 3+4=7. The natural boundary conditions reduce it to 3+2=5.

spline.title: An unpenalised line
spline.prompt: What is the integrated squared second derivative of g(x)=4−3x on any bounded interval?
spline.answer: It is zero, because the second derivative of an affine function is identically zero.

squared-error-is-not-the-logistic-likeli.title: Gradient sign
squared-error-is-not-the-logistic-likeli.prompt: With y=0 and output 0.99, why should a descent step reduce the logit?
squared-error-is-not-the-logistic-likeli.answer: The negative-log-likelihood gradient is +0.99x. At x=1, subtracting a positive step reduces the logit and hence the predicted probability of one.

squared-error-is-not-the-logistic-likeli.title: Same target, different loss
squared-error-is-not-the-logistic-likeli.prompt: Can squared error and Bernoulli log loss have the same optimal unconstrained population probability?
squared-error-is-not-the-logistic-likeli.answer: Yes. Both are minimised at the true conditional success probability, although their gradients and constrained sample fits can differ.

squared-error-of-an-average.title: A negative weight
squared-error-of-an-average.prompt: Weights that sum to 1 include a negative weight. Does the algebraic identity still hold, and can the ensemble error then exceed the weighted average of the member errors?
squared-error-of-an-average.answer: The identity still holds, because the cross term vanishes whenever the weights sum to 1. The disagreement term can be negative, so the ensemble error can exceed that weighted average.

squared-error-of-an-average.title: Best versus average
squared-error-of-an-average.prompt: Does the identity guarantee that an ensemble beats its most accurate member on each case?
squared-error-of-an-average.answer: No. It bounds the ensemble error by the average member error, not the smallest member error.

statistic-and-estimator.title: A statistic with an unknown distribution
statistic-and-estimator.prompt: Does dependence of $K$'s binomial distribution on $p$ disqualify $K$ as a statistic?
statistic-and-estimator.answer: No. Its formula $K=\sum_iX_i$ uses only observations; the sampling law may depend on $p$.

statistic-and-estimator.title: One point on the risk curve
statistic-and-estimator.prompt: At p = 1/4 and n = 4, compare the squared-error risks of (K+1)/6 and K/4. Does that comparison rank the two rules at every p?
statistic-and-estimator.answer: At p = 1/4, (K+1)/6 has variance 1/48 and bias 1/12, so its risk is 1/36 = 0.027778. The rule K/4 has risk 3/64 = 0.046875. At p = 0 the unbiased rule has risk 0, so one value of p does not rank the rules at every p.

stratified-and-cluster-sampling.title: Population weights
stratified-and-cluster-sampling.prompt: A region is 80% of the population but only half the sample. What weight does its sample mean get in the ordinary stratified population-mean estimator?
stratified-and-cluster-sampling.answer: It gets weight 0.8. The estimator uses population shares, not the fraction of sampled cases.

stratified-and-cluster-sampling.title: A two-stage design
stratified-and-cluster-sampling.prompt: A survey randomly selects villages and then randomly selects households inside each chosen village. Is this one-stage cluster sampling?
stratified-and-cluster-sampling.answer: It is a two-stage cluster design. One-stage cluster sampling would observe every household in each selected village.

studentised-coefficient-pivot.title: A contrast with a known scale factor
studentised-coefficient-pivot.prompt: The residual standard deviation is s = 2, a contrast satisfies cᵀCc = 1/2, and the estimated contrast exceeds its null value by 1.2. What is the Student statistic on 5 residual degrees of freedom?
studentised-coefficient-pivot.answer: The denominator is 2√(1/2) = 1.414214, so the statistic is 1.2/1.414214 = 0.848528 on 5 degrees of freedom.

studentised-coefficient-pivot.title: Independent pieces
studentised-coefficient-pivot.prompt: Why does zero covariance of the fitted coefficient error and residual suffice in the proof?
studentised-coefficient-pivot.answer: They are jointly Gaussian linear transformations of the errors. For jointly Gaussian vectors, zero cross-covariance implies independence.

sum-to-zero-and-contrast-constraints.title: An invariant comparison
sum-to-zero-and-contrast-constraints.prompt: The model is recoded without changing its column space. Does its residual sum of squares change?
sum-to-zero-and-contrast-constraints.answer: No. Least squares projects onto the same column space, so its fitted values and residual sum of squares are unchanged.

sum-to-zero-and-contrast-constraints.title: Is it a contrast?
sum-to-zero-and-contrast-constraints.prompt: Are coefficients $(1,-2,1)$ a contrast of three group means? What about $(1,1,1)$?
sum-to-zero-and-contrast-constraints.answer: The first sum is $0$, so it is a contrast. The second sum is $3$, so it is an overall linear combination rather than a contrast.

summary-statistics.title: A shifted sample
summary-statistics.prompt: A sample has mean $12$ and standard deviation $3$. Subtract $5$ from every observation. What are the new summaries?
summary-statistics.answer: The mean is $7$ and the standard deviation stays $3$. A common translation cancels from all deviations.

summary-statistics.title: Which spread?
summary-statistics.prompt: A report gives minimum $10$, first quartile $14$, median $16$, third quartile $19$, maximum $40$. Compute range and interquartile range.
summary-statistics.answer: The range is $40-10=30$; the interquartile range is $19-14=5$. The two numbers describe endpoints and the central half, respectively.

surrogate-split.title: Routing versus impurity
surrogate-split.prompt: Must the best surrogate also have the largest decrease in outcome impurity?
surrogate-split.answer: No. A surrogate is chosen to reproduce the primary left/right allocation; primary split selection evaluates the actual response.

surrogate-split.title: A reversed copy
surrogate-split.prompt: A candidate sends all eight cases to the opposite side of the primary split. After the allowed reversal, what are the agreement and the relative improvement?
surrogate-split.answer: Agreement is 8/8 = 1 and the relative improvement is 1. The original orientation would have scored agreement 0.

test-for-one-proportion.title: Choosing the variance
test-for-one-proportion.prompt: For $n=100$, $x=60$, and $H_0:p=0.5$, which standard error enters the score statistic?

test-for-one-proportion.title: A one-sided tail
test-for-one-proportion.prompt: If an upper test observes $x=7$, should its exact $p$-value include $X=8$?
test-for-one-proportion.answer: Yes. Every outcome at least as large as $7$ belongs in the upper tail, including $8$.

tests-and-confidence-intervals.title: A matching level
tests-and-confidence-intervals.prompt: Which confidence level pairs with a two-sided test of size $0.01$ when the same acceptance rule is inverted?

tests-and-confidence-intervals.title: A one-sided alternative
tests-and-confidence-intervals.prompt: Which confidence set matches a test that rejects very large positive values of $(\bar x-\mu_0)/\mathrm{SE}$?
tests-and-confidence-intervals.answer: A lower confidence bound: values below the lower bound are rejected, while all sufficiently large candidate means remain in the set.

tg5-cattle-studies.title: Data or prior precision
tg5-cattle-studies.prompt: If y=0.3 has variance 0.04 and the prior is N(0.1,0.01), which gets more weight in the conditional mean?
tg5-cattle-studies.answer: The prior precision is 100 and the data precision is 25, so their weights are 0.8 and 0.2.

tg5-cattle-studies.title: Counting independent studies
tg5-cattle-studies.prompt: One study contributes four marbling estimates. Does that automatically give four independent studies?
tg5-cattle-studies.answer: No. They are four estimates within one study and may share animals and sampling error.

the-beta-distribution-is-the-two-categor.title: Binary count update
the-beta-distribution-is-the-two-categor.prompt: A Dirichlet(1,1) prior sees counts (2,5). What is the posterior mean of P1?
the-beta-distribution-is-the-two-categor.answer: The posterior concentrations are (3,6), so its mean is 1/3.

the-limit-of-hotelling-s-statistic.title: Two calibrations
the-limit-of-hotelling-s-statistic.prompt: Does the chi-squared limit imply that $T^2$ has a chi-squared law for every normal sample size?
the-limit-of-hotelling-s-statistic.answer: No. Normal sampling gives an exact scaled $F$ law; the chi-squared law is its fixed-dimension large-sample limit.

the-limit-of-hotelling-s-statistic.title: Estimated covariance
the-limit-of-hotelling-s-statistic.prompt: Why is independence of $S_n$ and the mean unnecessary for the limiting argument?
the-limit-of-hotelling-s-statistic.answer: Convergence in probability of $S_n$ to a fixed matrix is sufficient for the joint Slutsky argument; no finite-sample independence is required.

the-reweighted-error-is-one-half.title: Weights after an exact round
the-reweighted-error-is-one-half.prompt: The current learner has weighted error 0.3. After its exact finite AdaBoost update, what is its weighted error?
the-reweighted-error-is-one-half.answer: It is 1/2: the total correct and incorrect unnormalised masses are equal.

the-reweighted-error-is-one-half.title: A neutral learner
the-reweighted-error-is-one-half.prompt: What are $\alpha$ and the new weight vector when the current error is $1/2$?
the-reweighted-error-is-one-half.answer: $\alpha=0$, so every multiplier is 1 and the weight vector is unchanged.

three-easy-confusions.title: Marginal versus conditional
three-easy-confusions.prompt: Why does integrating coefficients reduce the inverse-gamma shape by $p/2$?
three-easy-confusions.answer: The Gaussian integral over the $p$ coefficients contributes $v^{p/2}$, changing the variance kernel from $v^{-n/2-1}$ to $v^{-(n-p)/2-1}$.

three-easy-confusions.title: Two samplers
three-easy-confusions.prompt: Which variance distribution gives independent posterior pairs when followed by a conditional coefficient draw?
three-easy-confusions.answer: The marginal $p(v\mid y)$. Using $p(v\mid\beta,y)$ with the current coefficient gives Gibbs transitions and generally dependent pairs.

training-data-and-classifier.title: A classifier or a procedure
training-data-and-classifier.prompt: What is the distinction between $D\mapsto g_D$ and $x\mapsto g_D(x)$?
training-data-and-classifier.answer: The first map is a learning procedure; the second is the classifier after the training sample is fixed.

training-data-and-classifier.title: A perfect training fit
training-data-and-classifier.prompt: Why can two thresholds have identical zero training error but different population risks?
training-data-and-classifier.answer: They can disagree on predictor values absent from the training set that carry positive probability in the target population.

transformations-of-data.title: Back-transformation
transformations-of-data.prompt: If $\log Y$ is conditionally normal with mean $2$ and variance $1$, what are the conditional median and mean of $Y$?
transformations-of-data.answer: The median is $e^2$ and the mean is $e^{2+1/2}=e^{2.5}$. The mean requires the variance correction.

transformations-of-data.title: Reversing order
transformations-of-data.prompt: For positive measurements, does $g(x)=1/x$ preserve their order?
transformations-of-data.answer: It reverses order: if $0<a<b$, then $1/a>1/b$. It is still one-to-one on the positive half-line.

translation-to-another-common-notation.title: Two normalisers
translation-to-another-common-notation.answer: $A(c(\theta))=\log a(\theta)$; dividing by $a$ is subtracting its logarithm in the exponent.

translation-to-another-common-notation.title: A variance derivative
translation-to-another-common-notation.prompt: In which coordinate does $A\prime\prime$ equal the variance of the natural statistic?
translation-to-another-common-notation.answer: In the natural parameter coordinate $\eta$, subject to differentiation under the normalising integral. An arbitrary reparameterisation introduces chain-rule terms.

tree-size-and-pruning.title: Pricing an added split
tree-size-and-pruning.prompt: A binary split reduces total training loss by $2.5$ and adds one leaf. Which side wins when the leaf penalty is $3$?
tree-size-and-pruning.answer: The unsplit leaf wins: the risk improvement $2.5$ is smaller than the extra penalty $3$.

tree-size-and-pruning.title: Depth versus leaves
tree-size-and-pruning.prompt: Does a penalty proportional to leaf count directly require every root-to-leaf path to be short?
tree-size-and-pruning.answer: No. It prices the number of leaves. Trees with the same leaf count can have different depths.

two-factor-analysis-of-variance.title: Replication and error
two-factor-analysis-of-variance.prompt: Why does a $2\times2$ full-interaction design with one observation per cell have no error degrees of freedom?
two-factor-analysis-of-variance.answer: There are four observations and four cell-mean parameters, so the model fits every cell and leaves zero residual dimensions.

two-factor-analysis-of-variance.title: Unequal cell counts
two-factor-analysis-of-variance.prompt: A 2×2 layout has cell counts 2, 2, 2 and 5. Can the balanced orthogonal split of the treatment sum of squares be used unchanged?
two-factor-analysis-of-variance.answer: Unequal cell counts remove that balanced orthogonality. Sequential sums of squares can then depend on which factor is entered first.

two-proportion-z-test.title: Why pooling
two-proportion-z-test.prompt: Why is $(X_1+X_2)/(n_1+n_2)$ used for the equality test?
two-proportion-z-test.answer: Under equality both samples estimate one common success probability, and this weighted pooled proportion is its null maximum-likelihood estimate.

two-proportion-z-test.title: Pooled or averaged
two-proportion-z-test.prompt: For 10 successes in 20 trials and 40 successes in 180 trials, what is the pooled null proportion, and what is the unweighted average of the two sample proportions?
two-proportion-z-test.answer: The pooled proportion is (10+40)/(20+180) = 0.25. The unweighted average of the sample proportions is (0.5 + 40/180)/2 = 0.361111. The larger sample receives more weight in the pooled estimate.

two-pseudo-count-conventions.title: Uniform prior conventions
two-pseudo-count-conventions.prompt: For Beta(1,1), what are the mean-scale and mode-scale prior sample sizes?
two-pseudo-count-conventions.answer: They are 2 and 0, respectively. The uniform density has no unique interior prior mode.

two-pseudo-count-conventions.title: Posterior mean after one success
two-pseudo-count-conventions.prompt: With Beta(5,5) and one success in one trial, what is the posterior mean?
two-pseudo-count-conventions.answer: The posterior is Beta(6,5) and its mean is 6/11.

two-responses-one-person.title: Independent units
two-responses-one-person.prompt: One hundred patients each provide two outcomes. How many independent patient-level contributions enter a clustered sandwich under independent-patient sampling?
two-responses-one-person.answer: One hundred; both responses from the same patient belong to one contribution.

two-responses-one-person.title: Feasible Bernoulli association
two-responses-one-person.prompt: Bernoulli means are 0.2 and 0.8. What is the largest covariance and correlation allowed by the joint success bound?
two-responses-one-person.answer: The maximum covariance is 0.2−0.16=0.04; the common marginal variance is 0.16, so maximum correlation is 0.25.

two-sample-hotelling-t2-test.title: The dimension correction
two-sample-hotelling-t2-test.prompt: For $n_1=12$, $n_2=15$, and $p=3$, what are the two F degrees of freedom?

two-sample-hotelling-t2-test.title: A new set of units
two-sample-hotelling-t2-test.prompt: Every first coordinate is multiplied by $100$ in both samples. Does the classical statistic change if the covariance is transformed consistently?
two-sample-hotelling-t2-test.answer: No. This is an invertible linear coordinate change, and the covariance-weighted quadratic form is invariant.

two-sample-t-pivot.title: Degrees of freedom
two-sample-t-pivot.prompt: Independent normal samples of sizes 8 and 12 share an unknown variance. What is the pooled pivot degrees of freedom?

two-sample-t-pivot.title: Known variance
two-sample-t-pivot.prompt: If the common variance is known, what replaces the Student reference distribution?
two-sample-t-pivot.answer: Using the known standard deviation gives an exact standard normal reference distribution.

two-sample-t-test.title: Equal group sizes
two-sample-t-test.prompt: When two group sizes match, must pooled and Welch p-values match?
two-sample-t-test.answer: No. Their standard errors coincide, but their degrees of freedom generally differ.

two-sample-t-test.title: A nonzero null
two-sample-t-test.prompt: An estimated difference is 5 with standard error 2. What statistic tests a difference of 1?

two-state-continuous-time-chain.title: A rate is not a probability
two-state-continuous-time-chain.prompt: Can a transition rate equal $3$ per hour even though probabilities cannot exceed $1$?
two-state-continuous-time-chain.answer: Yes. The rate has inverse-time units and describes the coefficient of a short-time probability. A finite-time transition probability remains between zero and one.

two-state-continuous-time-chain.title: Changing the clock
two-state-continuous-time-chain.prompt: Both positive rates are doubled. What happens to stationary probabilities and to the exponential relaxation rate?
two-state-continuous-time-chain.answer: The stationary fractions stay the same because the common factor cancels. The relaxation rate $\alpha+\beta$ doubles.

underfitting.title: The parabola example
underfitting.prompt: Why can adding more noise-free observations of y=x² fail to make a straight line an adequate predictor?
underfitting.answer: The line family cannot represent curvature; more data do not add a quadratic term.

underfitting.title: Two large errors
underfitting.prompt: A model has similarly large training and validation losses. Does the small gap prove good prediction?
underfitting.answer: No. Both losses can be large because the fitted function misses useful structure or because the prediction problem has substantial noise.

uniformisation.title: A zero generator
uniformisation.prompt: For $Q=0$ and any $\gamma>0$, what are $R$ and $P(t)$?
uniformisation.answer: $R=I$, so every clock event is virtual and $P(t)=I$.

uniformisation.title: Tail control
uniformisation.prompt: If the omitted Poisson mass is at most $10^{-6}$, what does that guarantee for each computed transition probability?
uniformisation.answer: The nonnegative truncation error in each entry is at most $10^{-6}$. The missing mass of each row equals that omitted Poisson mass.

uniformity-depends-on-a-domain.title: A boundary is not infinite mass
uniformity-depends-on-a-domain.prompt: Is the uniform law on $(0,1)$ improper because the interval approaches a boundary?
uniformity-depends-on-a-domain.answer: No. Its constant density integrates to one; removing or including the endpoints changes no mass for this continuous law.

uniformity-depends-on-a-domain.title: The missing indicator
uniformity-depends-on-a-domain.prompt: Why must the transformed density include the transformed domain?
uniformity-depends-on-a-domain.answer: The Jacobian describes a local change of volume. Without the support indicator it assigns weight outside the image of the specified probability law and can change its total mass.

uniformly-most-powerful-unbiased-test.title: An excluded competitor
uniformly-most-powerful-unbiased-test.prompt: Why does the most powerful right-tail normal test not contradict UMPU optimality of the two-sided test?
uniformly-most-powerful-unbiased-test.answer: The right-tail test is outside the unbiased class for a two-sided problem: its power falls below its size at negative shifts.

uniformly-most-powerful-unbiased-test.title: The moment constraint
uniformly-most-powerful-unbiased-test.prompt: Why does a differentiable unbiased power function have zero derivative at the null?
uniformly-most-powerful-unbiased-test.answer: It has a minimum there. In the normal shift family that derivative is $E_0[Z\phi(Z)]$, so this expectation must be zero.

unit-root.title: Effect of a shock
unit-root.prompt: For $X_t=X_{t-1}+\varepsilon_t$, what is the effect at time $t+5$ of adding one unit to $\varepsilon_t$ while holding all other innovations fixed?
unit-root.answer: It is still one unit: the shock enters every subsequent level.

unit-root.title: Stationarity null
unit-root.prompt: A KPSS test rejects its stationarity null. Is that numerically the same null as an ordinary Dickey–Fuller unit-root null?
unit-root.answer: No. The null hypotheses differ; rejecting stationarity is not the same decision rule as rejecting a unit root.

univariate-t-test-as-a-template-for-t2.title: A lost sign
univariate-t-test-as-a-template-for-t2.prompt: If $t=-2$, what does $t^2$ preserve and what does it discard?
univariate-t-test-as-a-template-for-t2.answer: It preserves the magnitude of the standardised departure through the value $4$, while discarding that the sample mean lies below the null mean.

univariate-t-test-as-a-template-for-t2.title: Checking the degrees of freedom
univariate-t-test-as-a-template-for-t2.prompt: At $p=1$ and $n=12$, what $F$ distribution corresponds to the squared Student statistic?
univariate-t-test-as-a-template-for-t2.answer: $F_{1,11}$, matching the square of a $t_{11}$ variable.

universal-approximation.title: What depends on accuracy?
universal-approximation.prompt: Does uniform approximation guarantee one finite width that works for all continuous targets at every tolerance?
universal-approximation.answer: No. The existence quantifiers allow both width and weights to depend on the target and the requested tolerance.

universal-approximation.title: Bounded output
universal-approximation.prompt: Can a network whose final output is a logistic sigmoid approximate the constant $2$ uniformly to error below $0.5$?
universal-approximation.answer: No. Its output lies between $0$ and $1$, so its error relative to $2$ exceeds $1$ at every input.

universal-approximation.title: A jump and the uniform norm
universal-approximation.prompt: Every continuous function on $[0,1]$ is at least how far, in uniform error, from the step that equals $0$ on $[0,1/2)$ and $1$ on $[1/2,1]$?
universal-approximation.answer: At least $1/2$. A continuous value cannot stay strictly within $1/2$ of both $0$ and $1$ at the jump.

vapnik-s-radius-margin-bound.title: Radius versus diameter
vapnik-s-radius-margin-bound.prompt: If R=3 is the ball radius and gamma=1 is the one-sided margin, what full-diameter/full-width ratio enters?
vapnik-s-radius-margin-bound.answer: D=6 and rho=2, so D²/rho²=9, equal to R²/gamma².

vapnik-s-radius-margin-bound.title: The dimension cap
vapnik-s-radius-margin-bound.prompt: If ceil(D²/rho²)=30 and p=7, what is the bound?

variable-importance.title: Loss convention
variable-importance.prompt: A shuffle changes mean squared error from $4$ to $5$. What is the unscaled permutation importance?
variable-importance.answer: $5-4=1$ squared response unit. A relative score would instead be $1/4=25\%$.

variable-importance.title: A helpful shuffle
variable-importance.prompt: Held-out mean squared error is $0.20$. After one shuffle of a column it falls to $0.15$. What is the unscaled permutation importance?
variable-importance.answer: It is $0.15-0.20=-0.05$. A shuffle that lowers the observed loss produces a negative score. The sign describes that comparison for the fixed model.

variogram.title: Two conventions
variogram.prompt: If the variance of an increment is eight, what is the semivariogram?
variogram.answer: It is half the increment variance, so it equals four.

variogram.title: Stationary covariance identity
variogram.prompt: A weakly stationary process has variance five and lag-two covariance two. What is its lag-two variogram?

vector-response-regression.title: A corner of the Fréchet bound
vector-response-regression.prompt: Margins are 0.2 and 0.5 and the joint success probability is at its upper Fréchet bound. What are the other three cell probabilities?
vector-response-regression.answer: The joint success probability is min(0.2, 0.5)=0.2. The cells are 0.2, 0, 0.3 and 0.5. One cell is zero, so the odds ratio is undefined.

vector-response-regression.title: What robustness covers
vector-response-regression.prompt: Does a sandwich variance make a misspecified marginal mean correct?
vector-response-regression.answer: No. It addresses variance estimation under specified regularity when the mean estimating equation is correct; a wrong mean can make its expected residual nonzero.

ward-s-method.title: The size adjustment
ward-s-method.prompt: Two singleton points have squared Euclidean distance ten. What is their Ward increase?

ward-s-method.title: Coincident centres
ward-s-method.prompt: Can two nonidentical clusters have merge increase zero?
ward-s-method.answer: Yes. Their centres may coincide, making the squared centre difference zero.

warp-breaks-data.title: What is the cluster?
warp-breaks-data.prompt: Does changing a data-frame column name from wool to factory establish a factory-level sampling design?
warp-breaks-data.answer: No. A name change supplies no design evidence. The grouping variable must correspond to independent scientific sampling units.

warp-breaks-data.title: Reading the link
warp-breaks-data.prompt: A high-tension coefficient is $-0.5$ in a log-mean model. What comparison does $e^{-0.5}$ express?
warp-breaks-data.answer: It is the high-to-reference fitted mean ratio, conditional on the other model terms. It is not an additive difference in break counts.

which-functions-are-kernels.title: A negative diagonal
which-functions-are-kernels.prompt: A symmetric proposal has $K(a,a)=-0.2$. Is another input needed to show invalidity?
which-functions-are-kernels.answer: No. A one-input Gram matrix already has quadratic form $-0.2$ at coefficient $1$.

which-functions-are-kernels.title: Changing the sign
which-functions-are-kernels.prompt: If $K$ is valid, is $-K$ always valid?
which-functions-are-kernels.answer: No. For $K(x,z)=1$, the one-input Gram entry of $-K$ is $-1$, which violates nonnegativity.

why-the-raw-sum-of-squares-cannot-choose.title: The endpoint
why-the-raw-sum-of-squares-cannot-choose.prompt: For n distinct data points, what is the optimised within-cluster sum of squares at K=n?
why-the-raw-sum-of-squares-cannot-choose.answer: It is zero because each singleton centre equals its observation.

why-the-raw-sum-of-squares-cannot-choose.title: An apparent increase
why-the-raw-sum-of-squares-cannot-choose.prompt: A local K-means run at K=4 has larger cost than a run at K=3. Does this refute W4*≤W3*?
why-the-raw-sum-of-squares-cannot-choose.answer: No. The inequality concerns the global optima, whereas a local run may return a suboptimal partition.

wilcoxon-rank-sum-test.title: A null expectation
wilcoxon-rank-sum-test.prompt: With no ties, and sample sizes n=4 and m=6, what is the expected rank sum E(W)?

wilcoxon-rank-sum-test.title: Tied observations
wilcoxon-rank-sum-test.prompt: Why do identical midrank sums occur more than once in an exact permutation enumeration?
wilcoxon-rank-sum-test.answer: Different observation-index subsets can have the same sum; each subset still carries its own permutation probability.

wilks-theorem.title: Count restrictions
wilks-theorem.prompt: Why does testing one coefficient in a model with many nuisance coefficients usually give one chi-squared degree of freedom?
wilks-theorem.answer: Only one independent smooth restriction is imposed; nuisance parameters are estimated under both models and do not count as restrictions.

wilks-theorem.title: Boundary mass at zero
wilks-theorem.prompt: For the nonnegative-mean boundary example, the limiting law of D is half a point mass at zero and half a chi-squared law with one degree of freedom. What is $P(D=0)$?
wilks-theorem.answer: One half. The other half of the probability lies on the positive chi-squared component.
